To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

activities which require the learner to produce language at least at the sentential level are more likely to be associated with processing that is more conducive to language acquisition, while activities that are more likely to require the learner to click on buttons as a response are more likely to result in shallower processing.

the kind of mental processes subjects engage in when doing different CALL activities are connected to the kinds of mental processes that are likely to lead to acquisition, and that the kind of processing subjects do is connected to the kinds and amounts of button clicks they make while doing the activities.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how students process language input in a CALL environment.
CALL (computer-assisted language learning) and the question of whether or not it can be used as a pedagogical tool to enhance language acquisition.

the relationship between the mental processing of CALL activities and the kinds of processing that lead to language acquisition, as well as the relationship between the behavior that is observed in a computer classroom and the kinds of mental processing that lead to acquisition.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

activities which require language production are connected to more effective mental processing, and activities which require the use of buttons are not connected to more effective language processing.
the activities that require the most production at a sentence level are the most connected to processing that should lead toward acquisition.

activities that require the learner to produce language, and that require them to make a response that requires some kind of processing, will lead to more effective processing and more language acquisition.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the more the learner is required to process the language, the more effective the activity is likely to be for language acquisition.
we have found that the more complex the activity, the more complex the thinking that goes on.
we have found that the kind of processing one does while using CALL activities is connected to the type of activity.
The main takeaway from our work is that
there is a need to better understand the connection between the mental processing and the behavior in CALL.
the way in which the CALL activities are designed and implemented does have an impact on the mental processing that is connected to them.
the kind of processing we expect to see in a CALL activity does seem to be correlated to the kind of mental activity that we would like to encourage.
